first.rationale: I currently intend to test onboarding simplification because onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and prior evidence indicates that shorter onboarding and fewer signup fields improve early adoption. I will verify the two directly relevant records and the promotional-pricing record to assess whether competitor pressure changes the tradeoff. The experiment should track qualified revenue and downstream conversion, not just completion, to avoid optimizing low-value signups.

final.rationale: Run a standard, segmented experiment shortening onboarding, with completion, activation, time-to-value, 30-day retention, and qualified revenue as guardrails. The current declines in completion and activation directly match the prior benefits of shorter onboarding, including a confirmed 3% retention lift. Signup-field reduction can be considered only for SMBs because its evidence did not generalize and included a 1% retention decline. Do not pursue promotional pricing: although it produced an 18% qualified-revenue lift, the 12% retention decline and failure at the first renewal cycle make it unsuitable for sustainable growth.
